sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s master how to pass 2D arrays to methods like a pro! You’ll learn:

• How to declare method parameters for 2D arrays
• The difference between passing arrays vs. single values
• Practical examples to use right away

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine a 2D array like a spreadsheet - rows and columns full of data. When you pass this spreadsheet to a method, you’re giving it the whole grid to work with!

**How it works:**
• A 2D array is just an array of arrays
• Methods can accept them as parameters
• The method can then read or modify the entire grid

**Key syntax:**
• Method declaration: `void processArray(int[][] arr)`
• Call the method: `processArray(my2DArray)`

The method gets access to all elements - no need to pass each value separately!

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ 2D arrays are passed by reference - methods can modify the original
✓ Method parameters need `[][]` syntax for 2D arrays
✓ The array size doesn’t need to be specified in the parameter
✓ Works the same way for all data types (int, String, etc.)
✓ More efficient than passing individual elements

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use enhanced for loops for cleaner 2D array processing
Check for null arrays before processing
Document expected array dimensions in method comments
donts: Don’t forget the double brackets `[][]` in parameters
Don’t assume all rows have the same length
Don’t modify arrays unless you intend to change the original
sections.protip: Use `Arrays.deepToString(arr)` for quick debugging of 2D arrays!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Passing Two-Dimensional Arrays to Methods used in real apps?

examples.how: Pixel data is stored in 2D arrays and passed to filters/transform methods
Game boards (like chess or tic-tac-toe) are 2D arrays passed to game logic methods
Cell data is passed as 2D arrays to calculation/formatting methods

problem.description: Write a method `sumDiagonal` that takes a square 2D array and returns the sum of its main diagonal elements (from top-left to bottom-right).
hints: The diagonal elements have equal row and column indices (0,0), (1,1), etc.
Use a single loop that increments both row and column
Make sure to check the array is square first
problem.explanation: The method loops through each row and adds the element where row index equals column index. For a 3x3 matrix, this sums elements at positions (0,0), (1,1), and (2,2).

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Passing 2D arrays to methods is just like passing 1D arrays - use `[][]` syntax
📌 Methods can read and modify the original array since it's passed by reference
📌 Practice with real examples like matrix operations or game boards
📌 You're now ready to handle multi-dimensional data in methods!
